messages:
pager-bot: :rotating_light: PAGING: High 5xx error rate and kv cache hit-rate collapse for tenant CobaltEdge in dedicated-pool-7. Triggered by prefetched-prefix eviction spikes. Incident ticket INC-2103 created.
maya: I'm on it. Confirming impact — telemetry shows 5xx spike started ~6m ago, tail latency up across most requests to that pool. CobaltEdge customer reported errors.
jordan: grabbing logs from pool nodes now. Looks like massive prefix churn — lot of small prefixes from the tenant hammering the shared prefix index.
lee: @maya can we isolate the tenant to avoid cross-tenant pollution? We have isolation knobs for dedicated pools but need a quick plan.
maya: Yes. Plan A: disable prefetch for CobaltEdge + evict their hot prefixes from shared cache, then pin them to their tenant-local cache. Plan B if that fails: shift their traffic to a standby pool and reprovision.
sarah: How risky is disabling prefetch? Any downstream latency hit?
jordan: Prefetch disabled => slightly higher cold-start token latency for some flows but avoids polluting global prefix cache. Better than continued 5xxs.
eli: I'm ready to run commands. What's the exact command?
maya: Use the admin CLI:
```
redcli cache prefetch disable --tenant=cobaltedge --pool=dedicated-pool-7
redcli cache evict-prefix --tenant=cobaltedge --pattern="cobalt_*" --pool=shared-prefix-index
```
I'll run the first one after we coordinate.
eng-sre-bot: Auto-check: standby pool for CobaltEdge is dedicated-pool-9 (capacity 120 tokens/s). Current utilization 20%. Failover script available.
jordan: Logs show memory thrash on node d-p7-03 and d-p7-05, evictions/sec > 15k. TTL spikes (kv_ttl_ms) from 1200 -> 150. Likely config regression with recent rollout of prefetch heuristics.
maya: Ok executing disable now. @eli run the evict-prefix job after I confirm.
eli: Running evict job: job-id evict-210305-1. Output tail:
```
[evict-210305-1] evicting prefixes... 3421 entries removed, throttle applied
[evict-210305-1] complete: removed 3421 prefixes in 12s
```
eli: Verified command returned 0.
maya: Observability: cache hit-rate for CobaltEdge rising from 6% -> 82% on tenant-local cache, shared-prefix-index hit-rate recovering from 12% -> 45%. 5xx error rate dropping.
lee: Nice containment. Can we keep prefetch disabled until we validate the heuristic patch on staging?
jordan: I'll roll back the prefetch heuristic release on canary and run A/B tests. Suspect change in prefix grouping logic.
sarah: Customer ops notified?
maya: Support pinged CobaltEdge with immediate mitigation summary and ETA for next update. They reported reduced errors on their side.
eng-sre-bot: Incident timeline snapshot created at 2103057330, tagging leads maya/jordan.
eli: Suggest we also add a circuit-breaker in routing to avoid filling shared cache when tenant request rate > X rps. Filing a follow-up RFC.
maya: Agreed. For now, keep dedicated-pool-7 in monitoring and do a controlled restart of d-p7-03 early to clear any kernel-level memory fragmentation. I'll schedule the restart at +10m.
jordan: I'll watch for regression after restart. If hit-rate drops again, we fail over traffic to d-p9.
sarah: On-call handoff in 20m — @maya will hand to @lee. Leave full notes in the ticket.
maya: Copy. Updating INC-2103 with commands run, metrics, and next steps (rollback heuristic, routing CB, restart).
pager-bot: :white_check_mark: Severity reduced to P2 at 2103057390 — customer impact reduced, error rate within acceptable window. Monitoring continues.
lee: Taking over monitoring. Noted planned restart and rollback work. Thanks team.
maya: Nice quick work everyone. Postmortem to be scheduled; include hypothesis that aggressive prefetch heuristics caused prefix fingerprint collision leading to eviction storms.
eng-sre-bot: Reminder: attach logs from d-p7-03/d-p7-05 and evict-210305-1 output to INC-2103.
lee: Will do. Closing slack thread once oncall verifies steady-state for 1h.
